description:
User directed 2026-11-19: "add the elixir parity issues as tickets to the epic we gave to Elixir Parity". Owner: Elixir Parity. Found by Elixir Parity building fz-nhb.5. runtime/src/escape.rs:130 accepts \\x with one hex digit and \\x{H...}; Elixir (elixir_interpolation.erl:221-226) accepts only \\xHH and raises 'invalid hex escape character, expected \\xHH' otherwise, so fz accepts programs Elixir rejects. Predates nhb.5 (moved, not written). Done: \\x accepts exactly Elixir's forms; a self-check fixture covers the rejected ones.

Re-test on develop de4ef6a3b (Elixir Parity, 2026-11-24; user-approved update): the old premise was wrong. Elixir 1.19.4 accepts "\x4" and "\x{41}" with a deprecation warning; only "\xg" is an error, and fz's message there already matches. Done when: the same deprecation warning goes through the compiler's warning path (emit_warning_once), with a fixture carrying a .expected.diagnostics golden. Evidence: Elixir Parity's fresh/report.md.
title: Deprecated \xH and \x{H} escapes warn, as in Elixir
